artists.biography:
"Rhiannon Giddens"   the singer and multi-instrumentalist is best known as the frontwoman of African-American string band the Carolina Chocolate Drops, whose 2010 album Genuine Negro Jig earned them a Grammy Award for Best Traditional Folk Album. Raised in Piedmont, North Carolina, Giddens studied opera at the Oberlin Conservatory before relocating back home, where she became immersed in the rural musical traditions of that region. 
In 2013 Giddens began pushing further into her solo career. Giddens participated in "Another Day, Another Time", a concert inspired by the Coen brothers film Inside Llewyn Davis. Many critics have stated that Giddens had the best performance at what was called "the concert of the year".

perplexity.description:
Rhiannon Giddens' Freedom Highway, released in 2017 on Nonesuch Records, is a powerful blend of Americana, folk, and old-time music, with subtle inflections of jazz, blues, and world traditions. The album features nine original songs written or co-written by Giddens, alongside a traditional tune and two civil rights-era covers: "Birmingham Sunday" and the Staple Singers' "Freedom Highway," which gives the album its title. Recorded in Louisiana in historic wooden rooms, the production—co-led by Giddens and Dirk Powell—emphasizes acoustic textures, with Giddens' expressive vocals, banjo, and handclapping at the center, supported by a small ensemble that includes trumpet, mandolin, and percussion.

Freedom Highway marks Giddens' second solo studio album, following her acclaimed 2015 debut Tomorrow Is My Turn. While her debut focused on reinterpretations of songs by influential female artists, Freedom Highway showcases Giddens' own songwriting, reflecting on themes of history, identity, and social justice. The album was nominated for Album of the Year at the 2017 Americana Music Honors & Awards, cementing Giddens' reputation as a leading voice in contemporary roots music. Critics praised its emotional depth, historical resonance, and Giddens' ability to bridge genres and eras with authenticity and grace.
